title: Additive derived scalar extension with base scalar compatibility
statement: Let R and B be commutative rings, with B an R-algebra [def-weil-module-base-change]. Choose derived categories D(R) and D(B) [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with common morphism universe and module carriers in a universe containing both rings. Assume the ordinary extension functor is additive. There exist an additive functor L:D(R)\to D(B) and a counit L\circ Qh_R\to Qh_B\circ (-\otimes_R B) exhibiting L as the total left derived functor. For every R-complex E, integer i and r\in R, H^i(L(Qh_R(r\,id_E))) equals multiplication by the image of r in B on H^i(L(Qh_R(E))).

proof.text: Resolve the restricted R-complexes by K-flat complexes using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], specialized to ordinary modules on the one-point site. Extension to B sends quasi-isomorphisms of these resolutions to quasi-isomorphisms: this is the fixed-second-factor construction [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with second factor B in degree zero. Apply [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] to extension on the homotopy category followed by the derived localization. It supplies the functor L, the counit, its left-derived universal property, and computation on K-flat resolutions. These arguments allow unequal ring universes by lifting the coefficient rings to the common module universe and transporting along the canonical equivalences.

On K-flat models ordinary extension preserves sums and transports multiplication by r to multiplication by its image in B. Transport these equalities along the functorial resolution comparison isomorphisms. Additivity and the scalar equation then hold on all derived objects; applying the additive homology functor gives the asserted cohomological scalar equation.
